Senses.Explanation: (正) upright/correct + (中) within/amid + (來) come, coming: "coming from within the upright." Caoshan's own record pairs the graphs with the ruler-minister figure: "the lord is the upright position, the minister the inclined position..." (君為正位。臣為偏位。臣向君是偏中正。君視臣是正中偏, T47n1987A). It is the third of the Five Ranks (五位) that Dongshan Liangjie composed as the (五位君臣頌) in his own record, where (師)。(作五位君臣頌云) is followed by (正中偏) · (偏中正) · (正中來) · (兼中至) · (兼中到); his verse-line for this rank runs (正中來)。(無中有路隔塵埃)。(但能不觸當今諱)。(也勝前朝斷舌才) (T47n1986B). In the corpus it is chiefly deployed two ways. (1) As a fixed catechism-question: (如何是正中來) occurs 102 times in 56 texts, each master supplying a capping phrase — (師曰)。(徧界絕纖埃) (五燈會元), (松瘁何曾老)。(花開滿未萌), (屎裏翻筋斗), (獼猴戴席帽), and so on. (2) As a lemma the commentators gloss: "...is the attaining of the body of the teaching, and is also the upright position" (正中來一位，即是得法身，亦即是正位, X72n1437); the same text calls it "...one who enters the upright position and turns the body" (入正位而轉身者也) and another "...the pivot of the Five Ranks," (正中來，乃五位之樞紐 the position the first two ranks enter and the last two issue from, X72n1441). One (五燈全書) (上堂) maps a single shout onto the ranks — (即此一喝)，(不帶名言)，(是正中來也) — and then restates them (以濟宗論之): "...both person and object snatched away" (正中偏奪人也，偏中正奪境也。正中來，人境俱奪也, X82n1571). The graphs are the same across witnesses; the term carries no gloss here beyond the literal reading and its place in Dongshan's set.
Senses.Note: Corpus-wide sense (SenseKey null): 288 occurrences in 85 allowlist texts. (Counts are whole-file, tag-stripped with <note>/<rdg>/<orig> apparatus excluded; gate-2 recount, confirmed by two independent recounts.) The source verse is Dongshan Liangjie's own (T47n1986B, 瑞州洞山良价禪師語錄, 師。作五位君臣頌云…) — so that occurrence is attributed to him; the rest are the fixed (如何是正中來) catechism answered by various masters within lamp compilations (五燈會元, 五燈全書, 續燈正統) and analytical prose by later Caodong commentators — narrated/raised, MasterName null. This is the THIRD rank in Dongshan's canonical order (正中偏) · (偏中正) · (正中來) · (兼中至) · (兼中到); the ranks interrelate (see RelatedTerms). Note the neighbouring 4th-rank name is unstable across texts — (兼中至) (207×) vs (偏中至) (85×): X72n1437 records that (寂音) (Juefan Huihong) (改兼中至為偏中至)，(以對正中來) and calls the change (大悞後學); the 3rd rank (正中來) itself is stable.

Senses.Explanation: (正) upright / straight + (中) within + (偏) biased / tilted: "the biased within the upright." It is the first of the (五位) (Five Ranks) of (洞山良价) (Dongshan Liangjie), whose (五位君臣頌) opens with it: (正中偏)，(三更初夜月明前)。(莫怪相逢不相識)，(隱隱猶懷舊日嫌). (曹山本寂) (Caoshan Benji), asked the (五位君臣旨訣), supplies the corpus's own definition: (正位即空界)，(本來無物)。(偏位即色界)，(有萬象形)。(正中偏者)，(背理就事)。(偏中正者)，(舍事入理) — i.e. "(正中偏): turning the back on principle and going to affairs" (正中偏者，背理就事). In his ruler-minister scheme (君為正位，臣為偏位) he assigns it: "the ruler viewing the minister is (正中偏)" (君視臣是正中偏). It is deployed as a stock test-question — (如何是正中偏)？ — answered with a turning phrase (宏智正覺: 師曰：雲散長空後，虗堂夜月明). A later sermon maps the ranks onto Linji-school terms (以濟宗論之): (正中偏奪人也)，(偏中正奪境也). Beyond the graphs and these attested self-definitions the texts add no further gloss, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: The verse is (洞山良价)'s (五位君臣頌); the (背理就事) / (空界)·(色界) / (君臣) definitions are (曹山本寂)'s, given in answer to (五位君臣旨訣) — do not cross-attribute the verse and the gloss. Both are witnessed across ≥2 independent lamp records (禪宗正脉 X85n1593, 五燈全書 X81n1571) AND in the masters' own recorded sayings: the verse in (瑞州洞山良价禪師語錄) (T47n1986B), the (旨訣) answer in (撫州曹山元證禪師語錄) (T47n1987A). Pairs with and inverts (偏中正) (背理就事 vs 舍事入理; 君視臣 vs 臣向君). Member of the Five Ranks (五位) with (偏中正) · (正中來) · (兼中至) · (兼中到).

Senses.Explanation: Literally, the correct or proper command. The term occurs 1,503 times in 291 allowlisted texts. Chan records deploy it as the command that is issued, carried out, or fully brought forward by the person holding authority. Stock forms include 'the command is put into effect' (127 hits in 84 texts), 'fully bring forward the command' (170 in 103), and 'the command has already been carried out' (28 in 23). It appears in public questions about what the master will show when the command is in force, in appraisals of Yunmen's use of the staff, and beside military language of ruling within the realm and holding authority beyond the gate. One discourse also criticizes even 'raising the command's guiding principle' as making an artificial nest.
Senses.Note: The Zen bend is the transfer of governmental and military command language to the master's public seat, replies, staff, blows, and appraisals. The word names the command or order throughout; whether a passage praises or criticizes its deployment is not a second sense.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the true eye of the teaching
AlternateTargets: the eye of the true teaching
the correct eye of the teaching
Senses.Explanation: True or correct (正), teaching (法), and eye (眼): the true eye of the teaching. As a standalone term, distinct from 'treasury of the true eye of the teaching' (正法眼藏), the records say it is possessed, absent, brightened, or blinded. The forms 'possess the true eye of the teaching' (具正法眼, 15 occurrences) and 'better to possess the true eye of the teaching' (不如具正法眼好) name its possession. Its absence is described in the line 'one who does not possess the true eye of the teaching misses at every turn' (非具正法眼者，頭頭蹉過). Its presence verifies: 'if one possesses the true eye of the teaching, one will verify the nirvana-mind' (若具正法眼，必證涅槃心). The preface to Linji's record says that Linji illuminated the nirvana-mind by means of the true eye of the teaching (臨濟祖師以正法眼明涅槃心). It can also be blinded (瞎却正法眼). Most raw occurrences of the string belong to the longer compound 'treasury of the true eye of the teaching' (正法眼藏, 1,381 occurrences), so this entry is deliberately limited to the standalone eye. The standalone term also appears in direct test questions. In the repeated Ying'an–Mi'an case, Ying'an asks, 'what is the true eye of the teaching?' (如何是正法眼), and Mi'an immediately answers, 'a broken sand-pot' (破沙盆). This is distinct from questions about the longer 'treasury of the true eye of the teaching' (正法眼藏).
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide standalone sense. Every curated occurrence uses 'true eye of the teaching' (正法眼) without the following graph 'treasury' (藏). The longer compound 'treasury of the true eye of the teaching' (正法眼藏) has its own entry and is related literally as the treasury of this eye.

Senses.PreferredTarget: lineage-transmission phrase: the treasury of the true eye of the teaching
AlternateTargets: the true eye of the teaching treasury
the store of the true eye of the teaching
the treasury of the eye of the right teaching
Senses.Explanation: Literally the storehouse / treasury (藏) of the eye (眼) of the right teaching (正法) — in the record, the thing the lineage hands down. Its founding story is the World-Honored One on Vulture Peak holding up a flower before the silent assembly; only Mahakasyapa breaks into a smile, and the Buddha says (吾有正法眼藏)，(涅槃妙心)…(付囑摩訶迦葉) ('I have the treasury of the true eye of the teaching, the wondrous mind of nirvana... I entrust it to Mahakasyapa'). Thereafter each patriarch transmits it — (付囑於汝)，(勿令斷絕) ('I entrust it to you; let it not be cut off'), and a master speaks of his OWN transmitted teaching the same way: Linji on his deathbed says (吾滅後不得滅却吾正法眼藏) ('after I am gone, do not let my treasury of the true eye of the teaching be destroyed'), and when Sansheng answers with a shout, (誰知吾正法眼藏向這瞎驢邊滅却) ('who would have known my treasury of the true eye of the teaching would be destroyed at this blind donkey's side'). The term is questioned from within the record: Wumen presses the flower story with (正法眼藏作麼生傳) ('how is the treasury of the true eye of the teaching transmitted?') and argues that if you say it WAS handed over, the 'yellow-faced old man' (the Buddha) is cheating the villagers, and if it was NOT, why was Mahakasyapa alone singled out. In the corpus the phrase names the lineage's transmitted eye of the teaching, and masters both hand it down and put it in question. Two in-corpus self-definitions gloss the term directly: an annotation in (三峰藏和尚語錄) states (正法眼藏者)，(師師相傳之法眼也) ('the treasury of the true eye of the teaching: the eye of the teaching transmitted from teacher to teacher'), and the (重刻正法眼藏序) in (湛然圓澄禪師語錄) glosses the graph (藏) by simile — (正法眼藏者)，(難言也)，(請以喻明)。(譬如眼之洞見森羅萬象)，(取之無窮)，(用之無盡)，(故名曰藏) ('…like the eye's thorough seeing of the myriad forms, drawn on inexhaustibly, used without end — hence it is called a treasury'). The term is also deployed as a stock challenge, (如何是正法眼藏) ('what is the treasury of the true eye of the teaching?', 48x in 36 allowlist texts); recorded answers include Mi'an's (破沙盆) ('a broken sand-pot') in the case (應菴問密菴)：『(如何是正法眼藏)？』(密云)：『(破沙盆)。』 ('Ying'an asked Mi'an: what is the treasury of the true eye of the teaching? Mi'an said: a broken sand-pot' — raised repeatedly across the record), the single word (瞎) ('blind!', 破山禪師語錄), and (福昌重善)'s (夜觀乾象) ('watching the heavens by night'). Linji's deathbed phrase is itself re-raised across the record: (滅却)/(滅卻正法眼藏) ('destroying the treasury of the true eye of the teaching') recurs 17x in 14 texts. The texts add no gloss beyond this, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: This primary sense is the lineage's transmitted eye of the teaching, running from the Buddha's flower through the patriarchs to a master's own teaching. The separate title sense below covers the recut case collection. Zen-scoped raw-string counts remain 1,381 occurrences in 279 allowlisted texts; the challenge 'What is the treasury of the true eye of the teaching?' (如何是正法眼藏) occurs 48 times in 36. The word/title split does not alter those undifferentiated counts.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: (世尊曰) ('the World-Honored One said') — the lineage's own origin narrative (Wudeng Huiyuan, opening 七佛 'Seven Buddhas' / 釋迦牟尼佛 'Sakyamuni Buddha' section): the flower held up on Vulture Peak, transmitted to Mahakasyapa. The locus classicus of the term.

Occurrences.Kwic: 正法眼藏作麼生傳。設使迦葉不笑。正法眼藏又作麼生傳。若道正法眼藏有傳授。黃面老子誑謼閭閻。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (無門曰) ('Wumen says') — Wumen's comment on the flower case (Wumenguan case 6, 世尊拈花 'the World-Honored One holds up a flower'), questioning whether the treasury can be 'transmitted' at all.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我今以如來正法眼藏付囑於汝勿令斷絕。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The patriarch-to-patriarch handover formula in the Jingde Lamp Record: the eighth patriarch Buddhanandi (八祖佛陀難提) entrusts the treasury to his successor (伏馱蜜多) (Buddhamitra) — (付囑於汝)，(勿令斷絕) ('I entrust it to you; let it not be cut off'). Shows the lineage-continuation use; the transmitter is an Indian ancestor, not in the Chan-master index, so MasterName is left null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師臨遷化時據坐云：「吾滅後不得滅却吾正法眼藏。」三聖出云：「爭敢滅却和尚正法眼藏？」師云：「已後有人問爾，向他道什麼？」三聖便喝。師云：「誰知吾正法眼藏向這瞎驢邊滅却。」言訖端然示寂。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (師) = Linji, on his deathbed, calling his own transmitted teaching (吾正法眼藏) ('my treasury of the true eye of the teaching'); (三聖) (Sansheng Huiran) shouts, and Linji laments it will be 'destroyed at this blind donkey's side.' A master applying the term to himself. (Linji yulu.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 開堂示眾云。昔日靈山會上。世尊拈華。迦葉微笑。世尊道。吾有正法眼藏。分付摩訶大迦葉。次第流傳。無令斷絕。至于今日。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Section head (舒州白雲守端禪師); his inaugural sermon (開堂示眾) retelling the flower story and applying it — (次第流傳)，(無令斷絕)，(至于今日) ('handed down in succession, uninterrupted, to this day'). The living-lineage use. (Wudeng Huiyuan.)

Senses.PreferredTarget: book title: Treasury of the True Eye of the Teaching
Senses.Explanation: The exact graphs also name a book that can be gathered into fascicles, recut, and supplied with a preface. The heading 'Preface to the Recut Treasury of the True Eye of the Teaching' (重刻正法眼藏序) introduces a preface saying that Dahui selected material from the five houses, gathered more than one hundred masters into fascicles, and titled the resulting book Treasury of the True Eye of the Teaching (裒以成帙，目曰正法眼藏). The text then calls it 'this book' (是書也). A recut, prefaced book is a different referent from the treasury transmitted from teacher to teacher, although its title repeats the transmitted expression.
Senses.Note: The title witness is in the allowlisted Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng. Validation is provisional because this sense currently rests on one independent allowlisted work, although both its heading and prose identify the title. Not every occurrence inside the preface belongs here: the preface also discusses the inherited expression.

Occurrences.Kwic: 重刻正法眼藏序
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The division and head identify this as the 'Preface to the Recut Treasury of the True Eye of the Teaching,' anchoring the work-title referent.

Occurrences.Kwic: 故我大慧老人承悲願力，運無畏心，決擇五家，提挈最正者凡百餘人，裒以成帙，目曰正法眼藏。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The preface says Dahui selected more than one hundred masters, gathered the material into fascicles, and titled it Treasury of the True Eye of the Teaching.

Senses.Explanation: The graphs name a robe and an alms bowl. The allowlisted corpus has 513 hits in 115 texts, including records in which the objects are thrown onto a rock, lifted, carried, guarded, inventoried, or burned with a person’s other implements. Monastic regulations also name a ‘robe-and-bowl attendant’ (衣鉢侍者, 9 hits in 3 texts), who receives the seal in one installation procedure. In the Caoqi record, this attendant raises the robe associated with the object that could not be lifted at Dayu Ridge. These passages keep the material objects and their custodial office visible even where the same pair also marks succession.
Senses.Note: This first sense covers the material pair and its administrative extension to personal effects and the attendant responsible for them. It is separated from the succession-token sense because regulations can order the objects burned or placed in custody without describing succession.

Occurrences.Kwic: 盧見師奔至。即擲衣鉢於磐石曰。此衣表信。可力爭邪。任君將去。師遂舉之。如山不動。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Daoming account says Huineng threw the robe and bowl onto a rock, called the robe a token of trust, and Daoming could not lift it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 集眾燒衣鉢道具。遣逐偏門而出者。示耻辱也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The community-regulation section orders a dismissed person’s robe, bowl, and implements burned before expulsion through a side gate.

Occurrences.Kwic: 打印過，付衣鉢侍者收，知事全班列前上首。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An installation procedure assigns the seal to the robe-and-bowl attendant after it has been impressed.

Senses.Explanation: The pair also names the objects as passed evidence of succession. The corpus records ‘transmit the robe and bowl’ (傳衣鉢, 31 hits in 26 texts), ‘entrust the robe and bowl’ (付衣鉢, 10 hits in 8 texts), and one exact occurrence of ‘robe and bowl transmitted in succession’ (衣鉢相傳). The Dayu Ridge account explicitly calls the robe ‘a token of trust.’ Later addresses say that Huangmei’s robe and bowl were entrusted to Lu, while another asks which robe and bowl Lu actually transmitted. The question is recorded as a question rather than resolved here into an object different from the material robe and bowl.
Senses.Note: Historical succession does not make this a master-specific sense. The selected passages show the physical token, later transmission language, and a later challenge about what was transmitted. The seven required definition formulas were searched; no additional lexical self-definition was found.

Occurrences.Kwic: 爭似老盧無用處，却傳衣鉢振真風。大眾，且道那個是老盧傳底衣鉢？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wenyi’s address says that Lu transmitted the robe and bowl, then asks the assembly which robe and bowl he transmitted.

Occurrences.Kwic: 黃梅衣鉢，付與盧公。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An address in Xingduan’s section says that Huangmei’s robe and bowl were entrusted to Lu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曹溪守衣鉢侍者，因僧到，乃提起衣曰：者是大庾嶺頭提不起底。僧曰：為什麼却在上座手裏？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A collected case has Caoqi’s robe-and-bowl attendant identify the raised robe with the Dayu Ridge account, after which a monk asks why it is in the attendant’s hand.

Occurrences.Kwic: 衣鉢僅為師弟古卓老宿所藏。卓翁又終，其衣鉢相傳於南明之手十有餘年。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A lineage account says the robe and bowl were kept by one elder and then transmitted into Nanming's hands for more than ten years.
